name: U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz
status: Iran's diplomatic track reopened faster than expected. FM Araghchi met Qatari mediators in New York 28-29 Sep carrying a revised, narrower roadmap: a 4-5 day US timeline to release frozen Iranian funds, lift oil sanctions and end the naval blockade, with nuclear talks starting within 7 days -- a faster version of the 7-day roadmap Trump rejected 26 Sep. Araghchi expects a US response 'by Tuesday' (~30 Sep) and will return to Tehran once it arrives; a US official reiterated no war-ending deal without addressing Iran's nuclear program. Netanyahu traveled to the UAE 28 Sep to meet President Mohamed bin Zayed and reportedly met officials from other regional states without formal Israel ties, on Iran -- diplomatic, not kinetic. No new confirmed US, Israeli, Iranian or Houthi kinetic strikes this cycle. Saudi coalition intercepted 2 Houthi ballistic missiles and 2 drones headed toward Riyadh/Khamis Mushait on 26 Sep -- an attempted, not landed, strike, resolving the standing 21-day follow-on forecast CORRECT. Petroline: partial flow continues (newer reporting cites ~2.2M bpd, ~40% of a ~5.5M bpd baseline, versus earlier reporting of ~4M bpd against a 7M bpd nameplate -- the capacity figures are unreconciled across sources); full recovery still estimated 6-8 weeks out; attribution for the 10-11 Sep strike remains unclaimed. Yemen displacement still last confirmed at ~129,438 (21 Sep); WHO reports 800+ conflict deaths in Yemen fighting as of 28 Sep. Middle East crude exports reportedly rebounded to ~12.8M bpd in September, the highest since the war began in February.
importance: Critical -- a hard rejection reversed into renewed mediated engagement within 72 hours, and a formal US response is expected within days.
assessment: ASSESSED: the pace of re-engagement (rejection to a revised offer via a trusted mediator within three days) suggests both sides retain strong incentive to avoid escalation even as WSJ separately reports Trump is weighing post-midterm strikes -- these tracks are not mutually exclusive. Houthi attempted strikes continue independent of the Hormuz-focused channel, confirming the two fronts move on separate timelines.
lastChange: 2026-09-29 -- Iran returns with a revised, faster Qatar-mediated roadmap; Araghchi expects a US response by ~30 Sep. No new kinetic strikes confirmed. Saudi coalition intercepts an attempted Houthi strike on Riyadh/Khamis Mushait (26 Sep), closing the 21-day follow-on forecast CORRECT. Petroline capacity figures now conflict across reporting cycles (flagged as a gap).
orgRelevance: Track for a formal US response to the revised roadmap within 7 days; do not treat the reopened channel as resolution of the underlying blockade/Hormuz risk. Continue treating Hormuz and the Houthi-Saudi/Yemen track as two distinct risk lines.
nextIndicator: A formal US response (accept/reject/counter) by ~30 Sep-2 Oct; any Trump-Pezeshkian or higher-level direct contact; further Houthi attempted or landed strikes; Petroline full-restoration confirmation and reconciliation of conflicting capacity figures.

history.note: Operation Epic Fury begins the current conflict cycle.
Ceasefire collapses; Iran begins targeting Hormuz shipping.
IRGC ballistic-missile strike on Muwaffaq Salti/Al-Azraq air base, Jordan, intercepted by US/Jordanian Patriot PAC-3 batteries.
IRGC fires ballistic missiles at a U.S. carrier and destroyer (both evade); CENTCOM disables/destroys three Iranian tankers.
IRGC claims 8 Sep strikes on two U.S. Navy destroyers; CENTCOM calls the claim false; PGSA blacklist grows; transit at post-May lows.

IRGC claims an 11 Sep Saildrone-UUV strike; UKMTO reports two vessels hit off Oman; Acting Navy Secretary Cao confirms Bahrain base damage on the record; a 14 Sep GCC-Iran ministerial in Salalah is announced; Kpler/Lloyd's List transit data converges around ~12-13/day; unconfirmed East-West pipeline thermal activity surfaces near known flare sites.

Multiple drones from Iraqi territory strike the Petroline pipeline (10-11 Sep window); Saudi Arabia shuts the line as a precaution; investigation into the Iraq launch point opens; no claim of responsibility.

A new attack near Qeshm Island strikes an Iranian commercial vessel (IRIB: 1 killed, 4 injured) and UKMTO reports a separate vessel hit by an unidentified projectile; Abu Dhabi's Crown Prince meets Iranian President Pezeshkian at the BRICS summit in New Delhi — first top-level Iran-UAE contact of the war; Iran's nuclear chief is barred from traveling to the IAEA Vienna conference.

The 14 Sep Salalah ministerial is postponed 'in the interest of consensus'; CNBC publishes satellite imagery confirming the extent of Petroline pipeline damage; a bilateral Iran-Oman shipping-lane arrangement continues to be advanced separately.

Iraq dismisses the Maysan military commander and provincial police chief after an investigation into the Petroline strikes' Iraqi origin; IRI issues a non-denial; AP reports a 3-5 week repair estimate; the Salalah ministerial collapse is confirmed to stem from a substantive Saudi objection to the Iran-Oman proposal's wording, with no reschedule date set.

Iraq's own September deadline to disarm Iran-aligned militias is identified as running in parallel with, and complicated by, the Petroline-attribution investigation into those same networks; no new repair or reschedule data this cycle.

CENTCOM confirms an attempted Iranian USV seizure after six days of silence; a REPORTED U.S. strike destroys two IRGC boats (15 Sep); Houthis claim a Yanbu refinery attack; Iraq's security advisor walks back the 30 Sep disarmament deadline; Aramco reports a ~50%-within-days / full-in-4-6-weeks Petroline restoration timeline; CBO estimates the war has cost $38B through 1 Aug ($2-3B/month ongoing).

Trump tells Axios he faces a 'big decision' on whether to 'annihilate' Iran ahead of a Tuesday Gulf-leaders meeting at UNGA; IRGC claims striking/detaining the Togo-flagged tanker 'Trend', UKMTO logs a corroborating but unconfirmed incident; Yanbu refinery-vs-port-loadings status disputed between sources; Petroline restart still unconfirmed by Aramco.

Houthis fire ballistic/cruise missiles and drones at Riyadh and Aramco facilities at Yanbu, Taif, Baysh and Farasan (19 Sep); Saudi Arabia confirms the attempted ballistic-missile attack on its capital, the first of this cycle, with an Aramco-branded fuel tank burning near King Khalid International Airport and no casualties. Trump tells Fox News (20 Sep) the options are to 'wipe Iran out,' let the economy 'rot,' or make a deal. Pezeshkian and Araghchi arrive at UNGA (21 Sep) on U.S. visas with a leader meeting floated; markets ease. U.S. diesel sets a record above $6.50/gal. The 22 Sep Gulf-leaders meeting has not yet taken place.

Trump holds the 22 Sep Gulf-leaders meeting in New York; the postwar 'day-after' plan is REPORTEDLY deferred until after the November midterms. G7 foreign ministers issue a joint statement demanding the Houthis 'immediately cease all military actions' and calling on Iran to end its support; no independently confirmed new Houthi strike on Saudi territory since 19 Sep was identified, and the statement's apparent evidentiary basis traces to earlier September reporting. Pezeshkian departs for UNGA; no Trump-Pezeshkian meeting confirmed. Aramco has not confirmed a Petroline restart despite prediction-market pricing (~84.5%) favoring a partial restoration by ~30 Sep.

Witkoff and Kushner hold a three-hour direct session with Araghchi in New York (22 Sep); Trump calls it 'a lot of momentum,' Iranian state media states conditions (blockade lift, asset release, war termination), and a follow-on meeting is planned. Aramco achieves a confirmed partial Petroline restart (~4M of 7M bpd nameplate; full recovery up to six weeks). The Houthi Red Sea coast offensive is reframed as a widening Yemen ground war: 300+ Saudi strikes on Taiz/Hodeidah, UN displacement 86,000-130,000 trending toward a 230,000 forecast; no new confirmed Houthi strike on Saudi territory since 19 Sep.

CORRECTION: reporting and Iran's own MFA spokesperson confirm the 22 Sep session was indirect, via Qatari mediators, not a face-to-face direct meeting; Araghchi faces domestic Iranian backlash. UN Security Council press statement condemns continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia; OCHA-cited displacement confirmed past 130,000. No change to the ~4M bpd Petroline restart status.

Iran's written 60-day ceasefire roadmap (handed over 23 Sep) becomes public: a phased Hormuz reopening in exchange for ending the U.S. naval blockade and relief from secondary sanctions on Chinese energy buyers. Netanyahu tells UNGA that any deal preserving the Iranian regime would be a strategic failure -- a new, explicit veto point alongside Araghchi's domestic backlash. No formal U.S. response identified. Yemen displacement continues climbing toward the 230,000 forecast; Petroline status unchanged.

Trump rejects Iran's roadmap (now detailed as a seven-day Hormuz-reopening plan) on 26 Sep, calling its terms unacceptable; WSJ reports he is weighing renewed strikes after the November midterms. Reporting resurfaces that Netanyahu earlier called off a broader Iran strike after a Trump warning that Israel would be 'on its own.' Petroline attribution forecast closes CORRECT (unresolved through its window). No new confirmed Houthi strike on Saudi territory since 19 Sep; displacement still below 150,000.

Araghchi meets Qatari mediators in New York with a revised, faster Hormuz roadmap; expects a US response by ~30 Sep. Saudi coalition intercepts an attempted Houthi strike on Riyadh/Khamis Mushait (26 Sep), resolving the 21-day follow-on forecast CORRECT. Netanyahu visits UAE for Iran-related consultations (28 Sep). No new kinetic strikes confirmed.

name: CMMC Implementation
status: The Reform Task Force report has now missed a second informal target: trade press had cited ~28 Sep as an expected public-release date, and that date passed with no report and no new date given. DoD CIO Kirsten Davies has reaffirmed commitment to publishing without a firm timeline. DFARS 252.204-7012, NIST SP 800-171, SPRS scores and 7021/7025 remain fully in force. The FAR Overhaul's 19 Oct comment deadline is now roughly three weeks out and continues to draw on the same compliance-staff capacity.
importance: High -- a second consecutive slipped informal deadline; the compliance-calendar collision with the 19 Oct FAR comment deadline is tightening.
assessment: Policy pause, not repeal, remains the leading read. No evidence of a scope change behind the delay -- continued deliberation is the more likely explanation than an active decision to abandon the report.
lastChange: 2026-09-29 -- the ~28 Sep target passed with no report and no new date; DoD CIO Davies reaffirms commitment without a timeline. No Federal Register notice or departmental statement identified.
orgRelevance: Maintain 800-171/SPRS currency and C3PAO readiness through the continued gap; use the delay to finalize FAR Overhaul comment positions on the four September rules before the CMMC report adds a second compliance-calendar item.
nextIndicator: A Federal Register notice, class deviation, or 32 CFR Part 170 amendment; any new departmental statement with a firm release date.

history.note: DFARS acquisition rule effective; 252.204-7021/7025 added.
DoD suspends CMMC Phases 2-4 pending 60-day review.
Internal determination window (~11-13 Sep) arrives with no public output identified; reset planning to the ~28 Sep public report.
Trackers indicate the internal deliverable reached the DoW CIO on schedule but requires ~15 more days of synthesis; realistic public-report date resets to late September/early October.
No new development; public-report window remains late Sept/early Oct with no Federal Register or DoD statement this cycle.
Secondary/trade-press sources (CMMC Map) narrow the expected public-report date to ~28 Sep; internal determination's content remains non-public and no Federal Register action identified.

No new development on the CMMC report itself; a separate FAR Overhaul proposed rule (Parts 9/27/47, Federal Register 2026-19159) published the same day, creating a concurrent but distinct compliance-calendar item with a 19 Oct comment deadline.

No new CMMC development across the 18-21 Sep gap; the cited ~28 Sep public-report date is now a week out with no official confirmation. The concurrent compliance burden grew: the 18 Sep FAR Overhaul publication is confirmed to be four proposed rules covering eighteen parts, all closing 19 Oct, colliding with any CMMC response for the same staff.

No new CMMC development; report remains non-public. A continuing resolution signed 2 Sep funds the government through 11 Dec, giving compliance/contracts staff a stable near-term calendar to work both the CMMC report and the FAR comment deadline.
No new development; report remains non-public, still expected late Sept/early Oct. DFARS 7012/7021 and SPRS obligations unchanged.
No new development; report remains non-public. The FAR Overhaul's 19 Oct comment deadline and this report's expected late-Sept/early-Oct release continue to converge on the same compliance staff.
No new development; report remains non-public. DoD CIO Davies publicly reaffirms commitment to publishing it without giving a firm date.

No new development; report remains non-public past the cited ~28 Sep target. Confirmed the Task Force convened in early Sept to review 1,100+ RFI comments (assessment scope, cloud/MSP treatment, supply-chain implementation, OT applicability). FAR Overhaul's 19 Oct comment deadline is now three weeks out, ahead of the CMMC report's own timing.

The informally cited ~28 Sep public-report target passed with no report and no new date given; DoD CIO Kirsten Davies reaffirms commitment to publishing without a timeline. Second consecutive slipped informal deadline.

name: Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets
status: Post-summit assessment confirms the chokepoint is untouched. Analysts (CFR, Stimson Center, CNBC, The Diplomat) describe the 24 Sep Trump-Xi outcome as 'relief without resolution': no formal joint statement was issued (each side released separate statements), the operationalized US-China Board of Trade/Investment is characterized as producing 'limited and tentative' results, and Beijing offered only generic language on 'keeping global critical-mineral supply chains safe and stable' with no specific licensing commitment for military-affiliated firms. The military-affiliated licensing denial (since 1 Dec 2025), Decree No. 841 (effective 15 Sep, still no reported enforcement case), and the supplier-refusal pattern (gallium down ~65%, yttrium down ~98% year-to-date) all continue unchanged. China's rare-earth control-expansion suspension (10 Nov 2026) and the gallium/germanium/antimony suspension (27 Nov 2026) remain on track to expire inside a six-week window, converging with the 1 Jan 2027 foreign-entity-of-concern waiver cutoff.
importance: Critical -- confirms no near-term PRC relief just as a second, independent US-side production-capacity constraint (continuing-resolution funding levels blocking CCA production) becomes visible on a separate program, compounding the industrial-base squeeze.
assessment: ASSESSED: China's minimal-commitment approach at the summit preserves its rare-earth leverage into the 10/27 Nov suspension-expiry window. The operational conclusion is unchanged: licence status has stopped predicting delivery, and delivered material -- not the trade-truce headlines -- remains the correct risk gate.
lastChange: 2026-09-29 -- no new PRC action. Post-summit analysis confirms no rare-earth licensing relief surfaced; Board of Trade/Investment outcomes described as limited and tentative. A distinct US-side constraint (CR-level appropriations blocking CCA production) is now tracked in parallel on the Golden Dome/DIB thread.
orgRelevance: Re-confirm BOM/second-sourcing plans assume no near-term PRC relief; do not read the trade truce as supply-chain relief. Track the 10/27 Nov suspension-expiry cluster and the 1 Jan 2027 waiver cutoff as the near-term inflection points.
nextIndicator: Any PRC signal ahead of the 10 Nov or 27 Nov suspension expiries; first reported Decree No. 841 enforcement case; any joint-statement text surfacing with specific licensing language.

history.note: China imposes rare-earth export controls on 7 of 17 elements.
License denial extended to military-affiliated foreign firms.
China adds ten U.S. entities to its dual-use export control list, including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth.
CVN-81 steam-catapult/elevator redesign identified as a third magnet-demand vector; 10 Nov 2026 suspension-expiry ~2 months out.
No new PRC action; Iran's capture of a defective Anduril Dive-LD UUV near Hormuz surfaces a separate, narrow hardware-exposure risk vector.
No new PRC action; China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi confirms Xi's 24 Sep Washington visit, giving the thread a concrete near-term inflection date ahead of the 10 Nov suspension-expiry decision.
No new PRC action; analyst consensus (CSIS, Foreign Policy, S&P Global) converges on a one-year Busan-truce rollover as the summit's realistic outcome, not a rare-earth-specific resolution.

China's State Council exit-control regulation (effective 15 Sep) confirmed to bar rare-earth/battery/semiconductor engineers from leaving the country on a low evidentiary bar with no fixed time limit -- a new human-capital lever added to the licensing chokepoint.

Regulation confirmed in force; no enforcement case reported yet. New risk factor: China reportedly threatens to cancel the 24 Sep Xi-Trump summit over a pending $14B Taiwan arms sale, adding uncertainty to what had been an assumed stabilizing summit outcome.

Regulation identified precisely as Decree No. 841 (signed 22 Jul, effective 15 Sep), targeting rare-earth-separation, N-type solar, and EV-battery-electrolyte specialists; no enforcement case yet. Pre-summit commentary broadens from a single Taiwan-arms-sale threat to a multi-issue convergence (rare earths, tariffs, Taiwan, Iran) narrative.

Mechanism reassessed: Reuters-sourced reporting (4 Sep, unresolved since) describes Chinese suppliers refusing U.S.-bound shipments despite valid licences following Beijing's sanctioning of the Responsible Business Alliance, with gallium down 65% and yttrium 98% this year -- licence approval no longer predicts delivery. No Decree No. 841 enforcement case yet. The July 2026 executive order ends foreign-entity-of-concern waivers from 1 Jan 2027, closing the compliance escape route ahead of the 10 Nov 2026 suspension expiry.

No new PRC action; Xi departs for Washington with the summit framed by analysts as covering Taiwan/technology/trade rather than a specific rare-earth licensing gesture, and with China's own suspension not expiring until 10 Nov -- after the summit -- preserving its leverage.

No new PRC action; Xi arrives in Washington for a rare planeside Trump welcome ahead of the 24 Sep summit. Foreign Policy/Bloomberg framing confirms rare earths are on the formal agenda alongside AI, tariffs, Taiwan and Iran, but the structural timing (suspension expiry after the summit) argues against expecting licensing relief tomorrow.

Summit held; Bessent confirms the tariff truce is extended to 10 Jan 2027. No rare-earth licensing language for military-affiliated firms identified in the initial readout -- the structural timing argument (China's suspension expiring after the summit) held as tracked. A formal joint statement, if one follows, is the next test.

Post-summit analysis (The Diplomat, Washington Post) confirms no rare-earth licensing relief has surfaced; framed as 'relief without resolution' -- the trade-truce extension did not touch the constraint binding defense production. No new PRC action.

No new PRC action. Both Chinese suspension-expiry dates (rare-earth, 10 Nov; gallium/germanium/antimony, 27 Nov) are now inside six weeks, converging with the 1 Jan 2027 waiver cutoff. Confirmed U.S. Section 844 adds gallium/germanium to defense 'covered materials' sourcing restrictions effective 18 Dec 2027.

Post-summit analysis (CFR, Stimson, CNBC, The Diplomat) confirms no rare-earth licensing relief and 'limited and tentative' Board of Trade/Investment outcomes. No new PRC action. A second, US-side production-capacity constraint (CCA/CR funding) is now visible in parallel.

name: Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / Identity / AI-Infra CVEs
status: No new CISA KEV additions were identified since the 27 Sep Citrix NetScaler entries (CVE-2026-88771/88772); still no named DIB-sector or federal-contractor victim on any tracked CVE family (NetScaler, GitLab, Cisco FMC/ISE, F5 BIG-IP APM, SharePoint, WSO2, Adobe Commerce, MikroTik, Zyxel, Exchange). The exploited-surface class continues to widen beyond the enterprise edge: Apple shipped emergency patches (iOS/iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, macOS Sequoia 15.8.1) on 28 Sep for CVE-2026-86950, a CoreGraphics flaw Apple says 'may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals,' reported by Meta's security team -- mercenary-spyware-class targeting, not mass exploitation. Separately, security firm Cycode disclosed a CVSS 7.5 OAuth credential-theft flaw in Anthropic's own official MCP Python SDK (versions 1.9.1-2.1.1, GHSA-qx49-fqc8-xw99), fixed in 1.30.0/2.2.0 -- a flaw in AI-agent tooling's own client-side OAuth flow, distinct from the earlier LiteLLM/Bifrost AI-gateway KEV entries. A large crypto-exchange hack (Bitget, $351.6M-~$388M) is now claimed by the company to be linked to North Korea's Lazarus Group via a compromised third-party security product, though no independent technical attribution has been published; separately, Dutch police's ShinyHunters suspect (Pepijn van der Stap) appeared in a Rotterdam court 29 Sep, and Reuters independently verified some authenticity in ShinyHunters' claimed FBI-data leak.
importance: Critical -- the exploited-surface class now spans enterprise edge, mobile OS, and AI-agent tooling simultaneously, widening the combined patch-priority problem beyond any single vendor class.
assessment: ASSESSED: the multi-vendor edge/perimeter campaign tracked in prior cycles continues without resolution (no new KEV entries this cycle is a pause, not a stand-down, consistent with prior lulls that broke within days), while two genuinely new vectors -- targeted mobile-OS spyware and AI-agent-tooling OAuth theft -- confirm that identity-bearing attack surface is expanding into categories not previously tracked on this thread.
lastChange: 2026-09-29 -- no new KEV entries since 27 Sep; still no named DIB victim on any tracked CVE. New: Apple patches a targeted-spyware-class CoreGraphics 0-day (CVE-2026-86950); a CVSS 7.5 OAuth flaw is disclosed and patched in Anthropic's own MCP Python SDK; Bitget's ~$388M hack is claimed (unconfirmed) to be North Korea-linked; a ShinyHunters suspect appears in Dutch court.
orgRelevance: Patch all Apple devices to the 28 Sep point releases immediately, prioritizing executives and government-facing personnel. Upgrade any MCP Python SDK deployments past the vulnerable versions and bring AI-agent/MCP tooling into standard vulnerability-management scope alongside the enterprise-edge wave.
nextIndicator: Further KEV additions; any named DIB/federal-contractor victim; identification of the spyware vendor behind CVE-2026-86950; independent technical attribution of the Bitget hack.

history.note: Seven KEV additions (SonicWall, JFrog, LiteLLM, others).
CISA adds Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2026-19490) and Cisco FMC (CVE-2026-20079) to KEV amid a record Patch Tuesday.
CISA adds MikroTik CVE-2026-67277/CVE-2026-86060 to KEV, closing an 8-day gap; Cisco FMC and Citrix NetScaler carry a 12 Sep federal patch deadline — sixth vendor family in three weeks.
CISA adds CVE-2026-85706 (GitLab CE/EE path traversal, CVSS 10.0) to KEV.
watchTowr observes in-the-wild exploitation of the GitLab CVE within a day of disclosure; press coverage of Cisco Talos's FMC cluster attribution (published 9 Sep) continues.

Cisco Talos attribution — Sandworm-linked and Qilin-ransomware clusters exploiting Cisco FMC — confirmed as the most consequential development of this cycle; ~700 FMC instances remain internet-exposed industry-wide.
watchTowr/Rapid7 confirm GitLab CVE-2026-85706 exploitation has progressed to successful exfiltration of secrets and SSH configuration data from unpatched, internet-facing instances.
No new KEV additions or named DIB victim; both GitLab and Cisco FMC exploitation remain at a steady, unresolved risk level industry-wide.

CISA adds Cisco ISE (CVE-2026-76460), Cisco Secure Email Gateway (CVE-2026-76461, FCEB deadline today), Acronis Backup plugin (CVE-2026-87886), and Google Pixel modem (CVE-2026-58704) to KEV; WSO2 API Manager (CVE-2026-5430) reported under active exploitation via honeypot telemetry, not yet KEV-listed. CISA also announces discontinuation of its weekly Cyber Vulnerability Bulletin effective 28 Sep.

No new KEV additions confirmed for 17 or 18 Sep; Cisco ISE and Secure Email Gateway remain unpatched industry-wide; WSO2 confirmed still not KEV-listed; no named DIB-sector or federal-contractor victim identified for any tracked CVE (Cisco ISE, Secure Email Gateway, FMC, GitLab, NetScaler, WSO2).

CISA adds three actively exploited Linux kernel flaws to KEV (18 Sep): CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2025-39964 and CVE-2026-53266, with Red Hat confirming exploitation 19 Sep -- all local privilege escalation rather than remote entry. The Cisco ISE CVSS-10 federal remediation deadline (19 Sep) has passed with patches available; Cisco confirms it found the flaw via a customer support case, so at least one enterprise was compromised pre-disclosure though none is named. SolarWinds patches CVE-2026-28326 (hard-coded key, unauthenticated RCE) in ARM 2026.2.1 with no exploitation reported. WSO2 still unlisted. Thread direction changed to DEESCALATING at the perimeter, with priority moving to Linux hosts and privileged management tooling.

Reversal: CISA KEV-lists a Chinese-linked Zyxel GS1900 switch campaign (CVE-2026-7273, ~996 devices/48 countries, 21 Sep) and a zero-click Exchange Server RCE (CVE-2026-55007, federal deadline 22 Sep); Sophos documents an upgraded Sandworm-linked Cyclops Blink variant on compromised Cisco FMC devices. Both new KEV entries are network-facing, low-interaction vectors, directly contradicting the prior cycle's de-escalation call. Direction reverts to ESCALATING, indicator raised to RED. Still no named DIB-sector victim.

CISA adds four more actively exploited CVEs (22 Sep): Check Point Security Gateway/Spark pre-auth RCE (CVE-2026-85102, exploited since 12 Sep) and management pre-auth (CVE-2026-93616), Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-93952), and F5 BIG-IP APM (CVE-2026-94127, CVSS 9.8, discovered internally by F5, Friday 25 Sep federal deadline). Confirms the reversal is sustained across a second wave of vendors within 24-48 hours. Still no named DIB-sector victim.

No new KEV additions since 22 Sep. F5's Friday (25 Sep) federal deadline is one day out; still no named DIB-sector victim on any tracked CVE. The pause is treated as a likely reporting lull, not a resolution of risk.

F5 BIG-IP APM's federal remediation deadline lands today; fourth consecutive day with no new KEV additions. Still no named DIB-sector victim on any tracked CVE; pause remains assessed as a lull rather than resolution.

Lull broken: Citrix NetScaler zero-days CVE-2026-88771 (CVSS 9.5) and CVE-2026-88772 disclosed/patched 27 Sep after weeks of confirmed pre-patch exploitation (webshells) -- the third NetScaler-family KEV entry in three weeks. Separately, ten KEV additions across nine vendors landed 21-28 Sep including SharePoint (CVE-2026-65660), WSO2 (CVE-2026-5430), Adobe Commerce (CVE-2026-71362), and MikroTik (CVE-2026-67279). Still no named DIB-sector victim.

No new KEV entries since 27 Sep; still no named DIB victim. Apple patches a targeted-spyware-class 0-day (CVE-2026-86950); a CVSS 7.5 OAuth flaw is disclosed in Anthropic's own MCP Python SDK (GHSA-qx49-fqc8-xw99); Bitget's ~$388M hack is claimed (unconfirmed) to be North Korea-linked; a ShinyHunters suspect appears in Dutch court.

name: Golden Dome Procurement
status: The 29 Sep SASC Strategic Forces Subcommittee hearing ('To Receive an Update on Golden Dome') was held as scheduled, 4pm ET, chaired by Sen. Fischer with ranking member Sen. King. Witnesses per the Committee's own hearing page: CSIS's Thomas Karako, CBO's David Mosher, and -- newly identified -- David J. Trachtenberg of the National Institute for Public Policy. This directly seats the ~$185B-through-2035 (DoD) versus ~$1.2T-over-20-years (CBO) cost divergence before Congress, against a backdrop of DoD's reported repeated refusal of CBO briefing requests. Testimony content/outcome was not yet published as of this brief's compilation (same-day hearing). The SDA Tranche 1 Transport Layer A launch (21 Northrop Grumman-built satellites, Falcon 9 from Vandenberg SLC-4E) remains on schedule for ~00:00 UTC 30 Sep with no delay or scrub reported. Adjacent: L3Harris reportedly completed a preliminary design review for SDA's Tracking Layer Tranche 3 (18 satellites, $843M, FY29 launch target); Space Force reissued the SCAR ground-antenna program as a Commercial Solutions Opening (white papers due 15 Oct) after terminating a $1.7B AeroVironment prime contract earlier in 2026. Separately (parallel, not Golden Dome itself): the Air Force states the Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program is production-ready but cannot begin production under the current continuing resolution (FY26 levels through 11 Dec).
importance: High -- the cost-methodology dispute is now a matter of congressional record, and a distinct appropriations-level constraint (the CR) is confirmed blocking a separate flagship next-gen program, underscoring that funding mechanics, not just technology or materials, now gate production timing across multiple programs.
assessment: Procurement continues on schedule; the analytic centre of gravity remains the cost dispute, now formally before Congress. Sensing, ground and C2 layers continue to carry materially less cost-dispute exposure than the space-based-interceptor layer.
lastChange: 2026-09-29 -- SASC hearing held as scheduled with a third witness (Trachtenberg) identified; testimony/outcome pending publication. SDA Transport Layer A launch remains on schedule for 30 Sep. Space Force reissues SCAR as a Commercial Solutions Opening; L3Harris completes a Tranche 3 PDR. CCA production confirmed blocked by current CR funding levels -- a parallel, non-Golden-Dome data point on appropriations-level constraints.
orgRelevance: Watch the hearing transcript for interceptor-layer scope signals; the 15 Oct SCAR white-paper deadline is a near-term opportunity for ground-segment/SATCOM vendors. Track the 11 Dec CR expiry as a hard decision point for any funding-sensitive next-gen program, not just Golden Dome.
nextIndicator: Publication of the 29 Sep hearing testimony/transcript; the 30 Sep SDA launch outcome; any FY27 appropriations action ahead of 11 Dec; SCAR white-paper submissions (due 15 Oct).

Up to $3.2B in space-based-interceptor awards across 12 firms.
Classified USSF-153 launch (10 Sep) and SDA Tranche 1 Transport Layer A (30 Sep) confirm continued launch cadence.
No new award; Army's Valkyrie laser program redirected into the Navy-led E-HEL effort feeding Golden Dome's Joint Laser Warfighting System.

Guetlein states the program targets summer-2028 early operational capability; C2 'secret sauce' system under contract, passed two tests; lawmakers reportedly say they lack full visibility into program scope.

SASC Strategic Forces Subcommittee schedules a 29 Sep hearing on Golden Dome/missile-defense posture; no new award; 30 Sep SDA Tranche 1 Transport Layer A launch remains on schedule; no Gate 2/3/4 SBI update since early-August Gate 1 closure.

name: Pentagon DMDC Personnel Data Breach
status: DoD confirmed a breach of a Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) system exposing unencrypted PII -- names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, contact information, sex, race, and military occupational specialty data -- for approximately 3 million people (about 2.76M living, ~294,000 deceased). A small number of unauthorized users exploited a vulnerability in a file-sharing system between October 2025 and July 2026; DMDC discovered and patched the flaw 16 Jul 2026, but public disclosure came only 29 Sep 2026, a roughly nine-month undetected dwell time. No attribution (criminal vs. nation-state) has been made public.
importance: Critical -- a large-scale, sensitive-PII breach of a core DoD personnel system with a long undetected dwell time and inclusion of military-occupational-specialty data, which carries plausible counterintelligence value beyond routine identity-fraud risk.
assessment: ASSESSED: the breach's occurrence and rough scope are KNOWN (multiple independent outlets converge); attribution is UNKNOWN. The nine-month dwell time and the presence of MOS data are consistent with either an opportunistic criminal operation or deliberate state-sponsored collection, and public reporting does not yet distinguish between them -- this is the central uncertainty to resolve.
lastChange: 2026-09-29 -- thread opened. DoD confirms the breach and its approximate scope via multiple independent outlets (Time, Federal News Network, Cybernews); no attribution or full notification scope yet public.
orgRelevance: Any organization with veteran, reservist, or military-affiliated staff should assume some employees may be in the affected population. Brief HR/security on elevated identity-fraud and targeted-social-engineering risk; reinforce phishing-resistant MFA and identity-proofing for any process touching this population; do not attempt to independently verify individual exposure outside official DoD channels.
nextIndicator: DoD's formal individual-notification rollout; any attribution statement (criminal vs. state-sponsored); reports of downstream fraud or targeted social engineering against affected individuals; congressional or Inspector General inquiry announcements.

history.note: DoD confirms the DMDC breach affecting ~3 million people (intrusion Oct 2025-Jul 2026, patched 16 Jul, disclosed 29 Sep); unencrypted PII including SSNs and military occupational specialty data exposed. No attribution yet public.
